subtopic: Phi node placement at CFG merges
learningObjective: Determine correct phi placement and semantics at a control-flow merge involving multiple predecessors.
irSnippet:
; Non-SSA source (pseudo)
; if (cond) { x = a; } else { x = b; }
; return x;

; Candidate SSA lowerings:
bb_entry:
  br i1 %cond, label %bb_then, label %bb_else
bb_then:
  %x1 = ... %a
  br label %bb_merge
bb_else:
  %x2 = ... %b
  br label %bb_merge
bb_merge:
  ; ??? phi placement
  ret i32 %x_merged
stem: In the CFG shown, block bb_merge has two predecessors bb_then and bb_else, each defining a version of x (%x1 in bb_then, %x2 in bb_else). Which is the correct SSA representation of the merged value used in bb_merge?

options.text: Insert `%x_merged = select i1 %cond, i32 %x1, i32 %x2` at the top of bb_merge; select instructions replace φ nodes and are the canonical SSA construct for merging values.

Emit both %x1 and %x2 in bb_merge and let the register allocator pick which physical register holds the merged value at runtime; no φ is needed because SSA is only about textual assignments in the source block.
Duplicate bb_merge into two copies (one for each predecessor) so no merge exists; SSA cannot represent a value that has different definitions along different paths without CFG duplication.
Insert `%x_merged = phi i32 [%x1, %bb_then], [%x2, %bb_else]` at the beginning of bb_merge; the φ selects %x1 when control flow arrives from bb_then and %x2 when it arrives from bb_else.

explanation: SSA φ-functions at a merge point select the appropriate reaching definition based on the predecessor block from which control arrived. The correct LLVM syntax is `%x_merged = phi i32 [%x1, %bb_then], [%x2, %bb_else]` at the top of bb_merge. B is wrong (SSA requires the merge to be encoded in IR, not deferred to the register allocator). C is wrong (SSA does not require CFG duplication to represent joins). D is wrong at the SSA level: `select` requires both operands to be defined and both branches to have executed — it is a data-flow operation, not a control-flow merge; using select here would force evaluating both sides. E is wrong (OR is not a merge semantic).

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: `select` evaluates both operands and is a pure-data operation, not a control-flow merge. It is only equivalent when both branches can be safely evaluated (no side effects, no exceptions).
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: SSA requires the merge to be textually represented via φ; deferring to register allocation defeats the point of SSA.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: SSA handles joins with φ; duplication is neither required nor idiomatic.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: canonical SSA φ-placement at the merge with predecessor annotations.

assumptions: Both bb_then and bb_else complete and reach bb_merge; no exceptions or aborts.
LLVM IR conventions (phi at block top, block-annotated incoming values).
nonImplications: Does not imply select can never replace a φ; it can when the merged expressions are pure and side-effect-free and both branches are always safe to evaluate.
Does not imply φ has runtime cost; it lowers to copies during out-of-SSA.

distractorRationales.A: Confuses select data-flow with control-flow merge.
